nodes.summary: `Č(M, ε) ⊆ VR(M, 2ε) ⊆ Č(M, 2ε)` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Prop. 2.6).
nodes.title: The Rips–Čech interleaving

nodes.summary: `Č(M, ε) ⊆ VR(M, 2ε)`: points whose closed `ε`-balls share a point are pairwise at distance at most `2ε` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Prop. 2.6, first inclusion).
nodes.title: Čech inside Rips at twice the scale

nodes.summary: If `ε ≤ δ` then `Č(M, ε) ⊆ Č(M, δ)`, so the Čech complexes form an `ℝ`-persistence simplicial complex (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §2.3, the paragraph after Def. 2.9).
nodes.title: The Čech complex is a filtration

nodes.summary: For a (pseudo)metric space `M` and a scale `ε`, the Čech complex `Č(M, ε)` is the nerve of the family of closed balls `closedBall x ε`, `x ∈ M`: a nonempty finite set of points spans a simplex exactly when the closed `ε`-balls around them have a common point of `M` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §2.2, the construction `Č(V, ε)` with `V = M`, closed balls). The source does not say whether its balls…
nodes.title: Čech complex

nodes.summary: For `ε ≥ 0`, a nonempty finite set of points is a face of `VR(M, ε)` exactly when it is a clique of the `ε`-neighbourhood graph: the Vietoris–Rips complex is determined by its edges, which is the reason Carlsson gives for preferring it to the Čech complex (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §2.2, the paragraph before Def. 2.5).
nodes.title: The Vietoris–Rips complex is the clique complex of its one-skeleton

nodes.summary: For a family `U : ι → Set X` (for instance a covering of `X`), the nerve is the abstract simplicial complex on the index set `ι` whose faces are the nonempty finite sets of indices `s` with `⋂_{i ∈ s} U i ≠ ∅` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Def. 2.2).
nodes.title: Nerve of a family of sets

nodes.summary: `VR(M, ε) ⊆ Č(M, ε)`: if the pairwise distances of a nonempty finite set are at most `ε`, any of its points lies in all the closed `ε`-balls. With `2ε` in place of `ε` this is the second inclusion `VR(M, 2ε) ⊆ Č(M, 2ε)` of Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Prop. 2.6.
nodes.title: Rips inside Čech at the same scale

nodes.summary: If `ε ≤ δ` then `VR(M, ε) ⊆ VR(M, δ)` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §2.3, the paragraph after Def. 2.9).
nodes.title: The Vietoris–Rips complex is a filtration

nodes.summary: For a (pseudo)metric space `M` and a scale `ε`, the Vietoris–Rips complex `VR(M, ε)` has as faces the nonempty finite sets of points whose pairwise distances are all at most `ε` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Def. 2.5).
nodes.title: Vietoris–Rips complex

nodes.summary: Two distinct points are adjacent when their distance is at most `ε`; this is the one-skeleton of the Vietoris–Rips complex `VR(M, ε)` (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Def. 2.5 and §3.2).
nodes.title: The `ε`-neighbourhood graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
